title: Product design
description: Review the interaction, the chosen design system and the states a user must navigate.
questions: Which component or pattern in the chosen design system fits this interaction?
How will users recover from empty, invalid or interrupted states?
Can users complete the flow with a keyboard and a supported screen reader?

sources.title: GOV.UK Service Manual, Using moderated usability testing

specialists.title: Interaction designer
specialists.focus: Map the task across entry, decision, completion and recovery. Find steps where users could misunderstand scope, status or consequences.
checks: Each step shows status, consequences and a way back before an irreversible action.
Error and empty states are designed, not left to default messages.

specialists.title: Design systems designer
specialists.focus: Locate components and tokens in the project's chosen system. Compare composition and extension against adding a new pattern the team would need to maintain.
checks: Existing components and tokens are used before a new pattern is proposed.
A new component is documented with its states and usage rules in the design system.

specialists.title: Accessibility specialist
specialists.focus: Examine how keyboard, zoom and assistive technologies handle the relevant tasks. Identify focus behavior, accessible names and announcements in state changes.
checks: The task can be completed with keyboard only and at 200 percent zoom.
State changes are announced to screen readers and focus order follows the visual order.

specialists.title: Usability researcher
specialists.focus: Define representative participants and realistic tasks the team can observe. Separate usability observations from issues caused by prototype or test conditions.
checks: Participants match the target users and tasks are realistic, not leading.
Findings separate observed behaviour from participant opinions and prototype artefacts.

evidence: Current journey or prototype, target platform, available devices and the content the user sees at each decision.
The project's selected design system and version, existing components and screenshots or examples of their states.
Examples of slow, empty, invalid, interrupted or restricted states that occur in the actual workflow.
Recent user observations and applicable keyboard, focus, text resizing or assistive technology checks for the flow.
challenge: Compare an existing design system pattern with a simpler sequence or platform-native control. State which interaction and maintenance trade-offs justify a new component.
Walk the primary task with a keyboard and one relevant assistive technology configuration. Check where focus and error messages go after a failed submission.
Test what users infer before a destructive or irreversible step and how they resume when the flow is interrupted.
Check whether constrained space, long labels, text resizing or localization changes the reading or action order.
decision_criteria: Use an existing pattern when it communicates the correct task and states, passes relevant accessibility checks and fits the supported platforms.
Propose a new pattern only for a documented interaction gap. Specify its states, validation approach and maintenance owner.
Hold the current recommendation when an observed blocker prevents users from completing or recovering within the flow. Name the evidence that would resolve it.
Prefer a prototype or usability session when different designs make plausible but unverified claims about user understanding.
